chunks: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام that he said:

"Whoever performs one hundred rak'ahs in Masjid al-Khayf at Mina before departing from it, it equals the worship of seventy years. Whoever glorifies Allah therein one hundred times, Allah writes for him the reward like that of freeing a slave. Whoever declares Allah's oneness therein one hundred times, it equals the reward of giving life to a soul. Whoever praises Allah therein one hundred times, it equals the reward of the revenue of the two Iraqs being given in charity in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.إِحْيَاءِ نَسَمَةٍ: giving life to a soul; used here for immense reward
key_terms.تَحْمِيدَةٍ: an utterance of praising Allah, such as saying Al-hamdu li-llah
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَةٍ: an utterance of glorifying Allah, such as saying Subhan Allah
key_terms.تَهْلِيلَةٍ: an utterance of declaring Allah's oneness, such as saying La ilaha illa Allah
key_terms.خَرَاجِ الْعِرَاقَيْنِ: the revenue or yield of the two Iraqs, expressing vast wealth
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; for a God-pleasing charitable cause
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الْخَيْفِ: Masjid al-Khayf, the mosque in Mina mentioned as a place of special merit

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying and performing dhikr in Masjid al-Khayf at Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the immense reward of worship and dhikr in Masjid al-Khayf at Mina. It encourages salat, tasbih, tahlil, and tahmid in that sacred place by comparing them to great acts of devotion, liberation, and charity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.689 - Abu Hamza al-Thumali narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said:

"Whoever prays one hundred rak'ahs in the Mosque of al-Khayf in Mina before leaving it, it is equivalent to the worship of seventy years.
Whoever glorifies (says 'SubhanAllah (swt)') one hundred times in it, Allah (swt) records for them the reward of freeing a slave.
Whoever declares the oneness of Allah (swt) (says 'La ilaha illa Allah (swt)') one hundred times in it, it is equivalent to the reward of reviving a soul.
Whoever praises Allah (swt) (says 'Alhamdulillah') one hundred times in it, it is as if they have given in charity the value of the entire wealth of Iraq and its surroundings in the path of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic."
